t.2.105.1: Then Bharata, placing the two sandals upon his head, joyfully mounted his chariot, accompanied by Śatrughna.
t.2.105.3: Then, facing east, they went to the lovely river Mandākinī, keeping the great mountain Citrakūṭa on their right as they circled it.
t.2.105.2: Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, and Jābāli, firm in his vows, together with all the ministers honored for their counsel, went on ahead.
t.2.105.4: Then Bharata, together with his army, went on along its flank, beholding thousands of lovely and varied mineral veins.
t.2.105.5: Then, not far from Citrakūṭa, Bharata saw the hermitage where the sage Bharadvāja had made his dwelling.
t.2.105.6: Having reached that hermitage of Bharadvāja, the wise one, the delight of his family, alighted from his chariot and paid homage at the sage's feet.
t.2.105.7: Then the delighted Bharadvāja spoke these words to Bharata: "Has your task been accomplished, dear son, and has there been a meeting with Rāma?"
t.2.105.8: Thus addressed by the wise Bharadvāja, Bharata, devoted to dharma, replied to Bharadvāja.
t.2.105.9: Though entreated by his guru and by me, Rāghava, firm in his valour, greatly pleased, spoke these words to Vasiṣṭha.
t.2.105.10: I shall truly keep that very promise of my father, the promise my father made concerning the fourteen years.
t.2.105.11: Thus addressed, the greatly wise Vasiṣṭha, who knew the meaning of words, replied to Rāghava, himself skilled in speech, with words of great import.
t.2.105.12: O greatly wise one, gladly bestow these two gold-adorned sandals, which will secure your welfare and safekeeping in Ayodhyā.
t.2.105.14: Having been permitted by the most great-souled Rāma, I have turned back; taking the two auspicious sandals, I go to Ayodhyā itself.
t.2.105.13: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, Rāghava, standing with his face toward the east, gave me those two sandals wrought with gold for the sake of my kingdom.
t.2.105.15: Having heard this auspicious speech of the great-souled Bharata, the sage Bharadvāja uttered words more auspicious still.
t.2.105.16: This is no wonder, O tiger among men, best of those endowed with good character and conduct, that nobility should abide in you, just as rainwater settles in a low-lying place.
t.2.105.17: That mighty-armed Daśaratha, your father, is not dead, he whose son is one such as you, righteous of soul and devoted to dharma.
t.2.105.19: Then, having circumambulated Bharadvāja again and again, the glorious Bharata went on to Ayodhyā together with his ministers.
t.2.105.18: With palms joined in reverence, he clasped the feet of that great-souled sage, who had finished speaking, and began to take his leave of him.
t.2.105.20: And that vast army that followed Bharata turned back again, with its carriages and carts, its horses and elephants.
t.2.105.21: Then, having crossed the divine river Yamunā, garlanded with waves, they all once again beheld that river Gaṅgā of auspicious waters.
t.2.105.22: Having crossed that river, brimming with lovely waters, together with his kinsmen, he entered the delightful city of Śṛṅgaverapura along with his soldiers.
t.2.105.23: From Śṛṅgaverapura, Bharata once again beheld Ayodhyā, and, burning with grief, he spoke these words to his charioteer.
t.2.105.24: Charioteer, see: Ayodhyā lies ruined and does not shine; she is formless, joyless, wretched, her voices stilled.
